title: fix(attention test): give the DSV4 compressed mask test the cp axis rule
body:
# Description

- Under load-balanced context parallelism a sequence is split across devices and token order is shuffled, so the mask has to be built from token **positions** rather than row indices.
- `_load_balanced_context_parallel()` decides whether that applies by resolving `activation_q_length` against the *ambient* flax rules -- deliberately, so eval under `logical_axis_rules_for_eval` cannot claim an order the input pipeline never applied.
- `test_generate_attention_mask_compressed_load_balanced_context_parallel` never enters an `axis_rules` context, so the name resolves to `P(None)`, `cp_size` is 1, load balancing is skipped, and `AttentionType.COMPRESSED` returns a plain index-order mask while the test asserts the position-derived one.
- Fix: make that one rule ambient around the op and set `ulysses_context_sharding`, which the cp-size computation reads once the query axis resolves. Same bug and same fix as #5134, which landed just before this test was added.
- Only `activation_q_length` is made ambient, not the whole stub config: its `segment_ids_batch -> context` rule would shard this test's batch-1 segment ids across the 4-way context mesh.
- The test skips below 4 devices and is auto-marked `cpu_only`, so the 4-GPU `gpu-unit` job deselects it -- which is why CI has not been executing it at all.

# Tests

Reproduce the failure on `main` and the fix on this branch with:

    XLA_FLAGS=--xla_force_host_platform_device_count=4 python -m pytest \
      tests/unit/attention_test.py -k compressed_load_balanced_context_parallel

Verified on 4x AMD Instinct MI355X (ROCm 10, jax 0.11.1): fails on `main` (plain causal mask) and passes on this branch.

feat(ci): add fast-rebuild mode for Docker image pipelines
body: # Description Adds a `fast-rebuild` mode to the TPU and GPU Docker image pipelines (b/408067759). **Problem.** A code fix on a branch needs new CI images. A full build takes about 5 minutes per image, four images per pipeline. GitHub's "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the old image, but also the old code. **Solution.** `mode=fast-rebuild` copies the current code onto the images of an earlier run. The dependency layers stay the same bytes; only the code layers are new. The Docker build step drops from about 200 s to about 10 s per image. Fix: [https://b.corp.google.com/issues/408067759](https://b.corp.google.com/issues/408067759) ## How it works 1. `build_package` builds the wheel from the current commit. Unchanged. 2. New job `drift_guard`, on a GitHub-hosted runner, compares the source run's commit with the current commit. If `src/dependencies/`, `pyproject.toml` or `.dockerignore` changed, it refuses and lists the files. It also picks the overlay variant. 3. `build_and_push` looks up `:` in the registry, builds `FROM @` with the new code and pushes `:`. 4. CI tests, E2E tests and promotion use `:` exactly as before. A fast-rebuild run can be the source of the next one. | Variant | Chosen when | Docker build step | |---|---|---| | fast (`maxtext_code_overlay_fast.Dockerfile`) | no file under `src/maxtext/`, `tests/`, `benchmarks/` or `pytest.ini` was deleted or renamed since the source commit | 9 to 11 s, source image never pulled | | clean (`maxtext_code_overlay.Dockerfile`) | a file was deleted or renamed, or `src/maxtext/integration/vllm/` changed (post-training images) | 199 to 223 s, still exact | Security: the guard runs from the workflow's own checkout, never from `inputs.maxtext_sha`, and only reads the two commits as git data. ## Usage Manual only. `build-all` stays the default. The daily schedule and the release pipeline never use fast-rebuild. | Input | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `mode` | `build-all` | `build-all` is the full build as today. `fast-rebuild` copies the current code onto a previous run's images. | | `source_run_id` | empty | Required for `fast-rebuild`. The run whose images to reuse: the number after `actions/runs/` in that run's URL. | | `allow_dependency_drift` | off | Override. The guard refuses when dependency files changed since the source run, because the reused layers would no longer match a full build. Tick it to build anyway with a warning. Results may then differ from a full build. | | `repository_name` | `maxtext-images` | Existing input. The Artifact Registry repository the images are pushed to. Use a test repository for manual runs so nothing CI depends on is touched. | **From the GitHub UI** 1. Open the Actions tab and pick **TPU Docker Images Pipeline** (or **GPU Docker Images Pipeline**). 2. Click **Run workflow** and select your branch. 3. Set `mode` to `fast-rebuild`. 4. Set `source_run_id` to the id of the earlier run whose images you want to reuse. 5. Leave `allow_dependency_drift` off. Click **Run workflow**. **From the command line** ```bash # find the id of the earlier run gh run list --workflow tpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml --branch --limit 5 # start the fast rebuild gh workflow run tpu_docker_images_pipeline.yml --ref -f mode=fast-rebuild -f source_run_id= ``` Both start the same run, titled "Fast-rebuild from run ". Its images are `:` and the CI tests run on them as usual. Guide: `docs/development/ci_docker_image_pipelines.md`. Pointer from `docs/tutorials/build_maxtext.md`. ## Try it yourself Use a test `repository_name` (for example `maxtext-images-test`) on every run. Images then land in that repository instead of the production one, and nothing CI depends on is touched. About 40 minutes end to end, mostly CI test time. 1. **Baseline.** Same form, `mode=build-all`, `repository_name=`. Note the run id. Expect four "Build and Push Docker Image" jobs of about 5 minutes and the "Fast-rebuild Pre-flight" jobs skipped. 2. **Fast rebuild.** `mode=fast-rebuild`, `source_run_id=`, same `repository_name`. Expect the four pre-flight jobs to log `No dependency changes detected` and `Overlay variant: fast`, four build jobs of about 1 minute with a 10 s docker step, and the CI tests as in step 1. 3. **Chain.** Step 2 again with the step 2 run id as `source_run_id`. Same result. This is the everyday loop. 4. **Guard refuses.** Step 2 with the id of an old `main` run. Expect the pre-flight to fail in under a minute, list the changed files, and no build job. With `source_run_id` empty the run fails at "Validate fast-rebuild inputs". 5. **Re-run failed jobs.** On the step 2 run, click **Re-run jobs**, then **Re-run failed jobs** (or `gh run rerun --failed`). Expect attempt 2 to run only the failed CI shards, no pre-flight or build job, and each shard to pull `:` from the same repository again. The 14 pre-training shards fail again; they fail on `main` too. Needs the run's commit still on the branch. 6. **Clean variant, optional.** On a throwaway branch, rename a file under `tests/` and run step 2. title: fix: false-positive CI test duration regression alerts
body:
# Description

Resolves false-positive CI "Track Test Duration" regression alerts that have been failing every PR.

## Problem

The "Track Test Duration" job compares each test's duration against the last scheduled main run. `pytest-split` reshuffles tests across 3 workers on every run. The first test in each worker that uses a model family pays an XLA cold-compile cost (~30–130s), while subsequent tests reuse the cache (~4–25s). Because the layout changes every run, a different test absorbs the penalty each time, causing the CI to falsely report massive (300%+) regressions. This has failed on **15 out of 15** PR runs where the check executed.

## Root Cause Analysis

An investigation across 19 CI runs (15 PR + 4 scheduled main) confirmed that only two modules are affected: `moe_test` and `attention_test`. No other module has ever triggered an alert. The third-highest swing across all other modules is +12.8s — below the 15s absolute threshold.

Tests within these modules DO share compilation cache (3–10x speedup when a sibling runs first), contrary to the initial assessment that they generate completely unique computational graphs. The compile cost includes shared sub-computations (reference attention, MoE forward pass, mesh setup).

Previous attempts to fix this by adding `__hash__`/`__eq__` to `HyperParameters` and custom attention kernels were ineffective — `HyperParameters` is partialed out before jitting (never a jit argument), and the kernel classes already had proper pytree registration.

## Fix

1. **Per-test exclusion list for noisy modules:** Adds `EXCLUDED_MODULES_PER_TEST` in `process_test_results.py` containing `moe_test` and `attention_test`. Per-test regressions in these modules are logged as `::warning::` for visibility but do not fail the CI run.
2. **Full enforcement retained for all other modules:** All ~19 other modules (~46% of TPU test time) retain the original per-test regression enforcement with the same thresholds (20% relative AND 15s/30s absolute).
3. **Deterministic benchmark arrays:** Sorts the glob results and dictionary iterations in `process_test_results.py` for stable macro-level dashboard tracking.
4. **No workflow changes:** `track_performance.yml` is unchanged from main.

# Tests

- Added unit tests verifying excluded modules (`moe_test`, `attention_test`) return `failed=False` on regression.
- Added unit test verifying non-excluded modules return `failed=True` on regression.
- Added unit tests for skipped and failed testcase handling.
- Verified all 8 tests pass locally.
- Validated deterministic output array generation.

title: Onboard GLM-5.2
body:
# Description

This PR introduces native support for **GLM-5.2 Cross-Layer Index Sharing (IndexShare)** and **Indexer Parameter Pruning** in MaxText.

In GLM-5.2 (744B), sparse attention is shared across groups of decoder layers following a configurable topology (e.g. `FFFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSSFSSS` across 78 layers). Only 21 Full (F) layers instantiate indexers and compute query/key projections and Top-K sorting, while the remaining 57 Shared (S) layers reuse the cached indexer state (`indexer_mask`, `topk_indices`, `indexer_score`) with zero projection or sorting overhead.

### Key Changes and Technical Implementation:

1. **Cross-Layer State Carry in `nn.scan` and `NNXDecoder`:**
   - Modified `NNXDecoder._apply_layers_sequentially` and `scannable_block` to carry `cached_indexer_state = (mask, indices, score)` across scanned loop iterations.
2. **Conditional Execution in `MLA.__call__`:**
   - Implemented `jax.lax.cond` branching inside `MLA` to execute `_run_full` on Full layers and `_run_shared` (reusing the mask and indices without compute) on Shared layers.
3. **Physical Parameter Pruning (`prune_shared_indexers=true`):**
   - Skips initializing the `Indexer` sub-module and its weight parameters on the 57 shared layers, saving substantial memory footprint and eliminating unneeded weight transfers.
4. **Group-Normalized Loss Scaling:**
   - Normalized the auxiliary KL divergence distillation loss by `1 / group_size` across shared layer blocks, made fully compatible with dynamic JAX scan tracing.
5. **Head Chunking for Distillation Memory Optimization:**
   - Added `mla_qk_head_chunk_size` in `calculate_indexer_loss` using `jax.lax.scan` across head chunks to avoid large intermediate `[B, H, T, S]` allocations during training.
6. **Checkpoint Conversion and Donor Mapping:**
   - Added donor layer mapping in `param_mapping.py` to seamlessly convert and load HuggingFace GLM-5.2 checkpoints containing only 21 physical indexer tensors.

---

# Tests

- **Multi-Host TPU Pre-Training:**
  - Executed continuous pre-training steps with synthetic data on a multi-host TPU cluster.
  - Verified numerical stability: stable training loss and steady-state step times (`seq=2048`, `per_device_batch_size=1`).
- **Profiling and Trace Validation:**
  - Captured execution traces to verify named profiling scopes: `glm_full_layer_indexer` and `glm_shared_layer_index_reuse`.
- **Checkpoint Conversion and Parameter Mapping:**
  - Validated parameter key mappings for both 78-layer stacked and unstacked GLM-5.2 checkpoints.

---

title: [Fix] MoE DP reduce-scatter and logical axis sharding in vLLM serving path
body:
# Description

This PR closes the ~30% end-to-end serving performance gap between `MaxTextForCausalLM` and native vLLM (`MODEL_IMPL_TYPE=vllm`) when serving MoE models (e.g. `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`) with DP Attention and Expert Parallelism enabled (`enable_dp_attention=True`, `expert_parallelism=8`, `tensor_parallelism=1`).

### Root Causes & Changes
1. **Pass `scatter_results` to `fused_moe_func` in `RoutedMoE.fused_moe_matmul` (`src/maxtext/layers/moe.py`)**:
   - In `tpu-inference` (`tpu_inference/layers/vllm/interface/moe.py`), `fused_moe_func` is invoked with `scatter_results=is_attn_dp(mesh)` (`True` when DP attention is enabled). This instructs `moe_gmm_local` to perform a 2-way `psum` over `expert` followed by a `psum_scatter` (`reduce-scatter`) across the DP attention axis (`attn_dp` / `attn_dp_expert`), directly returning hidden states sharded on `P(ShardingAxisName.ATTN_DATA)` (`[num_tokens // dp_size, hidden_size]` per DP rank) and enabling multi-chunk communication-computation pipelining (`actual_chunk_size = moe_chunk_size * scatter_axis_size`).
   - Previously, `RoutedMoE.fused_moe_matmul` omitted `scatter_results` (defaulting to `False`), causing every MoE layer to execute a full 8-chip `all-reduce` (`jax.lax.psum`) over the entire `[num_tokens, hidden_size]` buffer (`33.55 MB` per layer at `8,192` tokens) and return an unsharded `P('data')` tensor that then had to be sliced back down to `P(ATTN_DATA)`.
2. **Gate `self.selected_experts` computation behind `return_routed_experts` (`src/maxtext/layers/moe.py`)**:
   - `RoutedMoE.fused_moe_matmul` previously computed a duplicate `jax.lax.top_k(gating_output, self.num_experts_per_tok)` and stored `self.selected_experts = nnx.Intermediate(top_k_indices)` unconditionally on every layer (even though `fused_moe_func` already computes `top_k` internally), which `Decoder.__call__` concatenated and returned from the JIT model on every step. Gating this behind `getattr(self.config, "return_routed_experts", False)` avoids redundant `top_k` and concatenation during standard serving.
3. **Add `'expert'` axis to `mlp`, `activation_mlp`, and `vocab` in `src/maxtext/configs/inference/vllm.yml`**:
   - When running with `tensor_parallelism=1, expert_parallelism=8` (`Mesh: attn_dp=1, attn_dp_expert=4, expert=2, model=1`), attention rules (`heads`, `kv_heads`, `gdn_head`, `activation_vocab`) map to `['model', 'expert']` (2-way sharded across `expert=2`), whereas `mlp` and `activation_mlp` previously mapped only to `['attn_dp', 'model']` (`1 * 1 = 1`) and `vocab` mapped to `[]`.
   - This left Qwen3.5 full-attention `out_proj` (`out_kernel_axis=("mlp", "embed_attn")`), all shared expert MLP weights (`shared_experts`), and the vocabulary projection weights completely unsharded (`P(None, None)`). Adding `'expert'` aligns their 2-way tensor sharding with the rest of the model.

BUGS: b/549307194

# Tests

End to End Benchmark (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` on TPU v7x-8, Multi-Turn Agentic GRPO Benchmark)

**Port note:** this is #5271 applied to `atwigg/mlperf`. An earlier revision of the same change landed on this branch as #5306 and was reverted in #5309; this is the version that merged to `main`.

The only deviation from #5271: the gated `selected_experts` top-k keeps this branch's fp32 softmax router probs (added in #5297 for router replay parity) instead of #5271's raw-logit top-k. Softmax is monotonic, so the indices are identical; all other files are byte-identical to #5271.

Test status on this branch: `tests/unit/fused_moe_qwix_test.py` all 15 pass. `tests/unit/router_replay_test.py` has 32 pass / 4 fail, and all 4 failures (`PaddingExcludedFromSoftmaxTest`, `ForcedRoutingGradientTest::test_fully_padded_token_has_zero_gradient`, `OutOfRangeExpertIdTest::test_out_of_range_id_is_masked_not_nan`) reproduce on `atwigg/mlperf` without this change — they are `get_topk` forced-routing issues untouched here.

title: feat(ci): run newly added tests on TPU7X in pull requests
body:
# Description

Pull requests now run only their newly added or modified tests on TPU7X, and skip the TPU7X job when no touched test can run there. Scheduled, `workflow_dispatch` and release runs still run the full suite.

Why: TPU7X runners are scarce, and most PRs touch no test that runs there. Today `tpu7x-tests` never runs on pull requests at all.

Definition of "runnable on TPU7X": a test the scheduled `tpu7x-*` flavors would collect and not skip. That is, it carries `tpu_only` (on the function, its class or the module's `pytestmark`) and does not carry `skip_on_tpu7x`. Everything else is auto-marked `cpu_only` by `tests/conftest.py` and never selected by the TPU flavors.

When it runs: on every push to a pull request (`pull_request` opened, synchronize, reopened; draft or not). Each run diffs the whole branch against its merge base with the target branch, so every test added or modified anywhere on the branch counts, not only the latest commit, and the same tests run again on each push until merge. A push that changes only docs or excluded paths, or that fails lint, docs build or the package build, does not reach the TPU7X job (existing gate). After merge, nothing PR-specific runs; the tests join the scheduled TPU7X suite.


Fix: [https://b.corp.google.com/issues/530220873](https://b.corp.google.com/issues/530220873)

Changes:
- `tests/utils/newly_added_detection.py`: new CLI (`python3 tests/utils/newly_added_detection.py --base <ref> [--require-marker M] [--exclude-marker M]`). Standard library only, so it works on the bare `ubuntu-latest` runner where importing the `tests` package fails. Reads pytest markers from the AST with the same inheritance pytest uses. Exits 2 when it cannot diff, so a broken checkout is not mistaken for "no tests changed".
- `.github/scripts/analyze_code_changes.sh`: sets `has_new_tests` from the CLI with `--require-marker tpu_only --exclude-marker skip_on_tpu7x`. A detection failure falls back to running the job.
- `.github/workflows/ci_pipeline.yml`: `tpu7x-tests` runs on pull requests only when `has_new_tests` is true. Other events are unchanged.
- `.github/workflows/run_tests_against_package.yml`: on a TPU7X pull-request run the pytest marker becomes `<flavor marker> and newly_added`. Removes the `git fetch --depth=1` that made the checkout shallow and broke the merge-base diff, and fails the job if detection finds nothing inside the container instead of passing on pytest exit code 5.
- `.github/workflows/run_tests_coordinator.yml`: one worker for `tpu7x-*` flavors on pull requests.

FIXES: b/530220873

# Tests

Unit tests (11 added, run in the CI `cpu-unit` job and locally):

```
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/newly_added_detection_test.py -v
```

Local checks of the gate script:

```
python3 -I tests/utils/newly_added_detection.py --base main --require-marker tpu_only --exclude-marker skip_on_tpu7x
EVENT_NAME=pull_request bash .github/scripts/analyze_code_changes.sh main
```

End to end on GitHub Actions, all against this branch:
- This PR (touches tests, none `tpu_only`): https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/maxtext/actions/runs/35180011877. `Detected has_new_tests=false`. The rest of that run is blocked by a pyink failure in `tests/unit/csa_streamindex_test.py` that comes from `main` (#5079).

title: Add basic RoPE implementation to m3 core
body:
# Description

Adds `maxtext.m3.core.rope.apply_rope`, the base rotary positional embedding for
m3, as a pure function rather than a module — RoPE holds no state and allocates
no parameters, so there is nothing to place on a mesh. Only the base variant
lives here; specialized variants (YaRN, LLaMA 3.1 extended context,
partial-rotary, mRoPE) belong in the model directories that need them.

Numerics match the legacy `RotaryEmbedding` bit-exactly — half-split ("rotate
half") convention, angles in float32, sinusoids cast to the input dtype before
the rotation — so migrated models reproduce legacy numbers rather than
approximating them.

Two intentional deviations from the design doc sketch:
- `positions` expands to `(batch, length, 1, 1)` so it broadcasts against
  `(batch, length, heads, head_dim)`; the sketch's `positions[..., None]` does
  not broadcast. Mismatched shapes now raise instead of broadcasting silently.
- `min_timescale` is exposed, matching the legacy `rope_min_timescale` config.

Second m3 PR, following the package scaffolding in #5291. Still not wired into
any MaxText entry point.

# Tests

New `tests/unit/m3/rope_test.py` covers RoPE's defining properties
(position-zero identity, norm preservation, relative-position invariance of
attention scores, packed sequences), bit-exact parity against the legacy
`RotaryEmbedding` at float32 and bfloat16, and argument validation.

Run on a v6e VM (`JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu` since these tests are CPU-only and the
conftest skips `cpu_only` tests on accelerator testbeds):

title: Optimize JAX flash attention for long sequences with a specialized path.
body:
Optimize JAX flash attention for long sequences with a specialized path.
This change splits the flash attention implementation into two paths based on a sequence length threshold of 4096:
- Short sequences (<= 4096) use the existing implementation.
- Long sequences (> 4096) use a new _flash_attention_block_masked_long_seq implementation. This path optimizes performance removing the duplicate QK^T fusions and augmenting the V tensor with a column of ones. This allows the logsumexp sum to be computed as part of the P @ V contraction, eliminating a reduce sum and improving performance.
Both paths are updated to correctly handle Grouped Query Attention (GQA) when q_groups > 1 by reshaping instead of unconditionally squeezing the head dimension.
Unit tests are added to verify the correctness of the long-sequence path.

title: Support vLLM mamba prefix caching in the Qwen3 GDN layer (mirror of #5305)
body:
# Description

Mirrors #5305 (`main`) onto `atwigg/mlperf`.

Under mamba prefix caching, vLLM checkpoints the recurrent state per block rather than keeping one resident slot per request. A request therefore resumes from the block covering its last already-computed token and writes to the block covering its last token, and the two differ whenever a step crosses a block boundary. `_mamba_block_table_slots` resolves both slots from the mamba block table on TPU; the ids are clamped because the kernel DMAs them with bounds checks disabled.

The block size comes from a declared `gdn_mamba_block_size`, which the vLLM adapter pins to the attention block size when `cache_config.mamba_cache_mode == "align"`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This supersedes the inline implementation added on this branch in 13f01432a** ("Support mamba prefix caching block tables and prevent unpaged GDN fallthrough"), which was a hand-port of an earlier revision of the same work. The slot arithmetic is unchanged — same `block_tables` reshape/slice, same `read_col`/`write_col` derivation, same clamp. What #5305 adds on top: the logic is extracted into a tested helper, the returned ids are cast to `int32`, and the align path is gated on `gdn_mamba_block_size` instead of an undeclared `getattr(self.config, "mamba_block_size", 256)`.
>
> This branch's own GDN work is preserved — block quantization, `get_weight_dtype`, and `conv_kernel_init` in `qwen3.py` are untouched. @andytwigg worth a look at the resolution, since it replaces your commit's version of that block.

# Tests

Run on CPU against this branch:

- `tests/unit/qwen3_gdn_mamba_slots_test.py` + `tests/unit/vllm_adapter_mamba_block_size_test.py` — 7 passed (the two suites #5305 adds)
- `tests/unit/configs_test.py` + `tests/unit/configs_value_test.py` — 126 passed, 120 subtests (covers the new `gdn_mamba_block_size` field against the base.yml/types.py cross-checks)

Not run: end-to-end serving on TPU. No accelerator was free, so the prefix-caching path itself is covered by the unit tests above and by the review already done on #5305, not by a live run on this branch.

Formatting note: `pyink` reports `qwen3.py` and `adapter.py` as needing reformatting on this branch, but both are already unformatted at `atwigg/mlperf` HEAD (regions at `qwen3.py:1481` and `adapter.py:325`, neither touched here). Left alone to avoid unrelated churn.

title: Support vLLM mamba prefix caching in the Qwen3 GDN layer
body:
# Description

Port of #5305 onto the `atwigg/mlperf` branch.

**This branch is not starting from zero.** `atwigg/mlperf` HEAD (13f01432a, "Support mamba prefix caching block tables and prevent unpaged GDN fallthrough") already carries an inline version of the same block-table lookup. This PR replaces that version with #5305's extracted and tested one, and plumbs the real block size through instead of guessing it. Andy's two other changes in that commit — the `RuntimeError` guard for a tuple `active_cache` reaching the unpaged path, and the removal of the `isinstance(active_cache, tuple)` fallbacks — are outside #5305's scope and are **preserved as-is**.

## Problem

Under vLLM's mamba prefix caching (`mamba_cache_mode="align"`), a Qwen3.5 rollout on the MaxText-native path dies on the first decode step:

```
File "maxtext/models/qwen3.py", line 913, in __call__
  recurrent_state, conv_state = active_cache.get_gdn_states()
AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'get_gdn_states'
```

`Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` decided whether vLLM is driving paged state by sniffing for `mamba_state_indices`, but align mode is precisely the mode where tpu-inference stops populating it (`tpu_inference/runner/tpu_runner.py:3220-3246`) — the slots are derived on-device from the block tables instead. So `use_paged_state` went False and the layer fell through to the MaxEngine branch, calling `get_gdn_states()` on the 2-tuple of paged state arrays vLLM handed it.

The on-device block-table lookup align mode expects exists in tpu-inference at `layers/vllm/custom_ops/gdn_attention_op.py:122-152` — but that is the **vLLM model path**. Loading MaxText natively overrides the architecture to `MaxTextForCausalLM`, so that code never runs.

## Changes relative to `atwigg/mlperf`

1. **Extract the slot math into `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet._mamba_block_table_slots`** (`src/maxtext/models/qwen3.py`). Align mode needs the read and write slots to **differ**: a request resumes from the block covering its last already-computed token and writes to the block covering its last token, so a later request hitting that cached prefix can pick up the checkpoint. The arithmetic is unchanged from the inline version; it is now a documented static method with direct unit coverage. `run_jax_gdn_attention` already takes `read_state_indices` for exactly this (`tpu_inference/layers/common/gdn_attention.py:50`).

2. **Take the block size from config instead of a hardcoded `256`.** The inline version read `getattr(self.config, "mamba_block_size", 256)`, but MaxText declares no `mamba_block_size` field, so that `getattr` *always* fell back to `256` regardless of what vLLM was actually configured with. This PR declares `gdn_mamba_block_size` on `Qwen3Next` (`src/maxtext/configs/types.py`) and has the vLLM adapter set it from `cache_config.block_size` when `mamba_cache_mode == "align"` (`adapter.py`). `generate_maxtext_config` already does this kind of vLLM→MaxText translation for sharding and MoE padding.

3. **Require `gdn_mamba_block_size` before taking the block-table path.** The gate on this branch was `mamba_state_indices is not None or block_tables is not None`; it is now `... or (mamba_block_size and block_tables is not None)`. Previously a non-align configuration whose `mamba_state_indices` happened to be missing would silently index with the wrong block size. It now falls through to the unpaged-GDN `RuntimeError` guard already on this branch, which fails loudly instead. In align mode the adapter sets the key, so the paged path is still taken.

4. **Tests and codecov** (`tests/unit/qwen3_gdn_mamba_slots_test.py`, `tests/unit/vllm_adapter_mamba_block_size_test.py`, `codecov.yml`).

5. **Formatting**: `qwen3.py` on `atwigg/mlperf` has pre-existing `pyink` violations in `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` that the pre-commit hook rewrites on any edit to this file. Those reformats are included so the hook passes; they are unrelated to the fix above.

Non-align behaviour is unchanged: the `mamba_state_indices` branch is the same code as before, and `gdn_mamba_block_size` defaults to 0.

## Testing

`tests/unit/qwen3_gdn_mamba_slots_test.py` + `tests/unit/vllm_adapter_mamba_block_size_test.py` — **7 passed** (CPU backend). Covers the read/write split across a block boundary, clamping into the rank-local range, per-DP-rank slicing of the block table, and both branches of the slot-selection gate in `__call__`. The block-boundary case is inherently a regression test for the pre-#5305 behaviour — it expects read block 11 and write block 12 for the same request.

pyink / codespell / yamllint clean.

pylint on this branch reports 3 findings in `src/maxtext/integration/vllm/maxtext_vllm_adapter/adapter.py` (`W0718` ×2, `C0415`) in the metadata-injection block at lines 327-336. These are **pre-existing on `atwigg/mlperf`** and untouched here — verified by running the hook against the unmodified base files. This PR net *removes* three pylint findings (one `C0301` from the inline code it deletes, two from the pyink pass); the file score goes 9.95 → 9.99.

## What is not verified

**Same caveats as #5305** — this has not been run on hardware.

1. **No end-to-end align run.** The index math is unit-tested against the formula in `gdn_attention_op.py`, but nothing here proves a prefix-cache hit actually resumes from the right recurrent state. That needs a real rollout with `--mamba-cache-mode align`.
2. **`attention_metadata.block_tables` for hybrid models.** The vLLM op assumes one block table serves both attention and mamba, which holds because align forces `mamba_block_size == block_size` (`tpu_platform.py:526`). The failing config has 4 kv-cache groups, so this is worth confirming rather than assuming — if the metadata carries the attention group's table, the column arithmetic here is right but the ids are not.
3. **`gdn_mamba_block_size` naming/placement.** Happy to move it if config owners prefer it elsewhere; it sits with the other `gdn_*` keys.

title: [Fix] MoE DP reduce-scatter and logical axis sharding in vLLM serving path
body:
# Description

This PR closes the ~30% end-to-end serving performance gap between `MaxTextForCausalLM` and native vLLM (`MODEL_IMPL_TYPE=vllm`) when serving MoE models (e.g. `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`) with DP Attention and Expert Parallelism enabled (`enable_dp_attention=True`, `expert_parallelism=8`, `tensor_parallelism=1`).

### Root Causes & Changes
1. **Pass `scatter_results` to `fused_moe_func` in `RoutedMoE.fused_moe_matmul` (`src/maxtext/layers/moe.py`)**:
   - In `tpu-inference` (`tpu_inference/layers/vllm/interface/moe.py`), `fused_moe_func` is invoked with `scatter_results=is_attn_dp(mesh)` (`True` when DP attention is enabled). This instructs `moe_gmm_local` to perform a 2-way `psum` over `expert` followed by a `psum_scatter` (`reduce-scatter`) across the DP attention axis (`attn_dp` / `attn_dp_expert`), directly returning hidden states sharded on `P(ShardingAxisName.ATTN_DATA)` (`[num_tokens // dp_size, hidden_size]` per DP rank) and enabling multi-chunk communication-computation pipelining (`actual_chunk_size = moe_chunk_size * scatter_axis_size`).
   - Previously, `RoutedMoE.fused_moe_matmul` omitted `scatter_results` (defaulting to `False`), causing every MoE layer to execute a full 8-chip `all-reduce` (`jax.lax.psum`) over the entire `[num_tokens, hidden_size]` buffer (`33.55 MB` per layer at `8,192` tokens) and return an unsharded `P('data')` tensor that then had to be sliced back down to `P(ATTN_DATA)`.
2. **Gate `self.selected_experts` computation behind `return_routed_experts` (`src/maxtext/layers/moe.py`)**:
   - `RoutedMoE.fused_moe_matmul` previously computed a duplicate `jax.lax.top_k(gating_output, self.num_experts_per_tok)` and stored `self.selected_experts = nnx.Intermediate(top_k_indices)` unconditionally on every layer (even though `fused_moe_func` already computes `top_k` internally), which `Decoder.__call__` concatenated and returned from the JIT model on every step. Gating this behind `getattr(self.config, "return_routed_experts", False)` avoids redundant `top_k` and concatenation during standard serving.
3. **Add `'expert'` axis to `mlp`, `activation_mlp`, and `vocab` in `src/maxtext/configs/inference/vllm.yml`**:
   - When running with `tensor_parallelism=1, expert_parallelism=8` (`Mesh: attn_dp=1, attn_dp_expert=4, expert=2, model=1`), attention rules (`heads`, `kv_heads`, `gdn_head`, `activation_vocab`) map to `['model', 'expert']` (2-way sharded across `expert=2`), whereas `mlp` and `activation_mlp` previously mapped only to `['attn_dp', 'model']` (`1 * 1 = 1`) and `vocab` mapped to `[]`.
   - This left Qwen3.5 full-attention `out_proj` (`out_kernel_axis=("mlp", "embed_attn")`), all shared expert MLP weights (`shared_experts`), and the vocabulary projection weights completely unsharded (`P(None, None)`). Adding `'expert'` aligns their 2-way tensor sharding with the rest of the model.

BUGS: b/549307194

# Tests

End to End Benchmark (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` on TPU v7x-8, Multi-Turn Agentic GRPO Benchmark)

title: [maxtext] Add block-diffusion CFT and SFT
body:
## Motivation

#4776 added the opt-in block-diffusion pre-training path. MaxText now needs a
focused text CFT and completion-only SFT integration before rollout,
distillation, replay, or RL behavior is introduced.

## Dependencies

This change follows and depends on:

- #4776 for MaxText block-diffusion pre-training; and
- google/tunix#1891 for target-aligned diffusion SFT batches and weighted
  trainer loss.

Both dependencies are merged. Current MaxText pins upstream Tunix commit
`a8d70582f1e2f1fb65973210989e0e148b5ef7ad`, a descendant of the Copybara
integration of google/tunix#1891 (`bd1b0f47606a8bfb5158fe17084503c16bb4a62e`).

## Scope

This PR adds only:

- opt-in Hugging Face text CFT and completion-only SFT for
  `training_objective=block_diffusion`;
- clean targets, role-derived completion eligibility, corruption masks, and
  explicit target-loss weights through the SFT pipeline;
- a MaxText-to-Tunix adapter for target-aligned diffusion batches and logits;
- weighted training and preaveraged evaluation metrics;
- safe trainer routing for diffusion gradient accumulation and internal neural
  network metrics; and
- fail-closed validation for prompt/completion layouts that would expose a
  later prompt to an earlier completion inside one bidirectional diffusion
  block.

It does not add DPO, multimodal or audio training, rollout, serving,
distillation, replay, or RL. Block-diffusion training continues to require an
unpacked Hugging Face text pipeline.

## Training contract

The pre-training logit and canvas contracts remain unchanged:

- `same_position` logits with an `all_masked` canvas; and
- `shifted` logits with a `seed_and_mask` canvas.

CFT corrupts and supervises all valid target positions. Completion-only SFT
keeps prompt tokens as clean context and corrupts and supervises completion
positions only. Because attention is bidirectional within a diffusion block,
each block must contain a prompt prefix followed by a completion suffix. A
later prompt may start at the next block boundary; an assistant-to-user
transition inside one block fails with an actionable error instead of leaking
future prompt text.

The Tunix adapter requires non-None position, segmentation, completion,
corruption, and loss-mask fields. It verifies mask shapes and ownership before
constructing a weighted `DiffusionTokenBatch`. Diffusion evaluation already
returns a globally weighted mean, so the SFT hooks do not divide it by the
evaluation-step count again.

Tunix NNX graph caching remains enabled for normal dense training and disabled
for MoE. It is also disabled for block diffusion when internal neural network
metrics are recorded, because those intermediate graph nodes mutate the cached
graph structure.

## Compatibility

`training_objective=causal_lm` remains the default. Its shifted targets,
MaxText SFT trainer, completion masking, metrics, and dense graph-cache path
are unchanged. Focused tests cover both objective routes and the existing
causal fallback behavior.

## Tests

The current-main replay passed the full CPU gate against the exact upstream
Tunix #1891 integration:

```text
399 passed, 98 skipped, 3 deselected, 219 subtests passed
```

The 98 skips are platform-specific. The three pre-existing Hugging Face
iterator integration tests are deselected locally because they require live
`datasets.load_dataset` access; the changed objective-selection tests in that
module pass.

The gate covers block-diffusion primitives and attention, CFT/SFT corruption,
role masks, prompt-leak rejection, Tunix batch and logits adapters, weighted
metrics, cache routing, configuration, causal regressions, and positive- and
zero-weight gradient accumulation. The Tunix adapter has 100% statement and
branch coverage.

Pyink, repository-equivalent Pylint 3.3.8 (`10.00/10`), Python compilation,
and `git diff --check` also pass. The guarded publisher reruns these
checks on freshly fetched MaxText and Tunix upstream commits before it may
push.

## Checklist

- [x] I performed a self-review of the focused CFT/SFT boundary.
- [x] Existing causal SFT behavior remains the default and has regression coverage.
- [x] Unsupported training modes and unsafe completion layouts fail closed.
- [x] No rollout, distillation, replay, or RL implementation is included.

Design document:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1N7KcCoAIErB2CV9EJ2G1u_mdN-AQgqwNUYSvM0mtqMI/edit

title: [Stacked PR 1/6] Import Tokamax GDN forward kernel
body:
# Description

This is **PR 1 of 6** in the stacked series enabling the Pallas Gated Delta Net (GDN) backward pass kernel in MaxText.

**This PR is a exact import of the upstream Tokamax GDN forward kernel — nothing else.** The reason for being a standalone pr is so that PR 2 becomes a reviewable diff. Previously PR 2 added ~2,700 lines of brand-new files with no baseline, so a reviewer had no way to see what MaxText changed relative to upstream. With this PR landing the unmodified upstream kernel first, PR 2 shows only our delta.

## Provenance

- **Source repository:** [`openxla/tokamax`](https://github.com/openxla/tokamax)
- **Revision:** `6303c141386c991ae32801c61d4757097d4b05fd` (`main` HEAD at time of vendoring)
- **Upstream path:** `tokamax/_src/ops/causal_conv1d_gated_delta_rule/`

These files were last modified upstream by `706f2010761ea1c28250410160590923dd7ab6e8`, so the content is identical at either revision.

Reproduce any file with:

```bash
curl -sfLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openxla/tokamax/6303c141386c991ae32801c61d4757097d4b05fd/tokamax/_src/ops/causal_conv1d_gated_delta_rule/<file>.py
pyink --pyink-indentation=2 --line-length=122 <file>.py
```

## Deviations from upstream (complete list)

A byte-verbatim copy cannot pass MaxText CI, so three categories of **mechanical, non-semantic** adjustment were applied. There are no other differences — **no executable statement differs from upstream**.

1. **`pyink --pyink-indentation=2 --line-length=122`** — 8 of the 9 files reflowed (upstream is 80-column, MaxText is 122-column). Tool-generated; `compute_conv1d.py` was already conforming.
2. **One `codespell` fix** — `gurantee` → `guarantee` in `compute_conv1d.py` (comment text).
3. **Narrow, per-file `# pylint: disable=` pragmas**, listing only what each file actually needs:

   | File | Pragma |
   |:---|:---|
   | `tiling.py` | *none — already 10.00/10* |
   | `compute_conv1d.py`, `compute_gdn.py`, `metadata.py`, `vmem_ldst.py`, `wrapper.py` | `missing-module-docstring` |
   | `config.py`, `memory_ref.py` | `missing-module-docstring,missing-class-docstring,missing-function-docstring,use-dict-literal` |
   | `pallas_mosaic_tpu.py` | `missing-function-docstring,unused-import` (after the module docstring) |
   | `pallas_mosaic_tpu.py` | `redefined-outer-name`, `broad-exception-caught` (inline) |
   | `wrapper.py` | `no-value-for-parameter` (inline) |

   The three inline pragmas are byte-identical to the ones PR 2 already carries, so PR 2 shows no churn on them.

Imports are deliberately left pointing at `tokamax._src.ops.causal_conv1d_gated_delta_rule`. PR 2 rewires them to `maxtext.models.kernels.gdn`, which is genuinely part of our delta and should be visible in PR 2's diff.

# Files Changed

Vendored verbatim into `src/maxtext/models/kernels/gdn/`:
- `compute_conv1d.py`
- `compute_gdn.py`
- `config.py`
- `memory_ref.py`
- `metadata.py`
- `pallas_mosaic_tpu.py`
- `tiling.py`
- `vmem_ldst.py`
- `wrapper.py`

Plus one unrelated cosmetic line:
- `src/maxtext/models/qwen3.py`: a blank line after the module docstring.

# Tests

- `pre-commit run pyink --all-files`, `pre-commit run mdformat --all-files`, and `pre-commit run --from-ref <merge-base> --to-ref HEAD` all pass locally (`codespell`, `pylint` 10.00/10, `pyink`).
- No behavioural tests apply: nothing in the tree imports these modules until PR 2.

title: [Stacked PR 6/6] Optimize GDN forward/backward Pallas kernels and add Head-Sharded & Sequence-Sharded Context Parallelism (CP)
body:
# Description

This is **PR 6 of 6** in the stacked series establishing the canonical Pallas Gated Delta Net (GDN) implementation in MaxText.

This PR completes the GDN stack on top of PR 5 (`#5098`), consolidating the optimized forward and backward Pallas kernels and introducing full **Head-Sharded and Sequence-Sharded Context Parallelism (CP)**:

1. **True Sequence-Sharded Context Parallelism (`cp_gdn.py`)**:
   - `halo_exchange_for_conv` and `halo_exchange_for_conv_bwd`: causal Conv1D boundary halo exchange of $K - 1 = 3$ pre-conv QKV tokens via `lax.ppermute` across `cp_axis`, with cross-rank packed document `segment_ids` masking.
   - `compose_local_from_t_inv`: pre-batched forward affine transition summary using cached $T_c^{-1}$ (`t_inv`) from the forward Pallas kernel, convolving only $K$ channels (`1/6`th of QKV) and folding across local chunks via an $\mathcal{O}(\log_2 N_c)$ pairwise tree reduction.
   - 0-GEMM backward transition matrix transpose ($\mathrm{d}M_{\mathrm{loc}} = M_{\mathrm{loc}}^\top$) from cached `"gdn_m_local"` and pre-batched state adjoint summary (`compose_bwd_local_from_t_inv`) with $\mathcal{O}(\log_2 N_c)$ tree reduction.
   - `incoming_grad_state`: $\lceil \log_2(D) \rceil$-step reverse Hillis-Steele prefix scan over `cp_axis` in $\mathcal{O}(1)$ HBM per device.

2. **Unified CP Routing in `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` (`src/maxtext/models/qwen3.py`)**:
   - Selectable via `gdn_cp_mode: "auto" | "seq" | "head"` (defaulting to `"auto"`).
   - `"auto"` uses Head-Sharded CP at `CP = 2` (where `num_groups: 2 -> 1` yields `103 ms` single-pass step latency) and automatically switches to Sequence-Sharded CP at `CP >= 4` (scaling to `63 ms` at `CP = 4`, `32 ms` at `CP = 8`, and `8.9 ms` at `CP = 32`).
   - Supports `cp_size > num_k_heads` (e.g. `CP = 8` with `num_k_heads = 4` and `CP = 32` with `num_k_heads = 16`).

3. **Pallas Forward & Backward Kernel Optimizations**:
   - Backward pass optimizations: native BF16 MXU execution, algebraic GEMM reductions, and multi-group grid (`(batch_size, num_groups, num_chunks)`).
   - Forward pass optimizations: fast transpose broadcasts, TPU dot safeguards, and stable triangular inversion.
   - Conditional VMEM BlockSpecs: `has_dht` and `has_dh0` are only allocated in `pallas_gdn_bwd_kernel` when initial/terminal recurrent states are present, preventing any VMEM regression in pure FP32 mode.

# Tests
- **Multi-Device CPU Suite**: All tests pass in `venv_maxtext/bin/pytest`:
  - `gdn_cp_test.py`: 7 passed (including 8-device mock scan).
  - `gdn_cp_head_sharded_test.py`: 5 passed (with 4-device emulation).
  - `gdn_bwd_pallas_test.py`: 19 passed (including `test_gdn_decoupled_conv1d_cp_axis_against_single_device` and `test_bwd_block_specs_and_symbolic_zero_dht_dh0_omission`).
  - `gdn_benchmark_test.py`: 6 passed.
  - `pyconfig_test.py`: 46 passed.
- **Hardware Verification on Cloud TPU v7x (`TPU7x`)**:
  - `4`-chip (`8` `TPU7x` TensorCores) multi-chip CP sweep (`CP = 1, 2, 4, 8` side-by-side) verified on Ghostfish hardware.
  - Full non-CP `gdn_benchmark_ghostfish_test` suite (all 6 tests, including 64K and 8K FP32/BF16) verified on Ghostfish hardware.

title: Refactor multi-domain PyGrain dataset mixtures to use MapDataset.mix
body:
# Description

Refactors multi-domain dataset mixtures in MaxText's PyGrain data loader (`get_datasets()` in `src/maxtext/input_pipeline/grain_data_processing.py`) to mix at the `grain.MapDataset` level (`grain.MapDataset.mix`) instead of converting each dataset component to an `IterDataset` prior to mixing.

### Problem Being Solved & Context
When scaling multi-domain dataset mixtures (e.g., 35 domains in ArrayRecord format) on large Cloud TPU clusters (e.g. 512-chip Cloud TPU v6e / 64 hosts), stock MaxText suffered from:
1. **Thread Pool Explosion**: Stock MaxText called `_apply_mapdataset_transforms()` on every domain individually before `grain.IterDataset.mix()`, instantiating $D$ independent `.to_iter_dataset()` reader thread pools per worker process ($D \times W$). With 35 domains and $W=8$ workers across 64 hosts, this resulted in **17,920 thread pools** actively reading mmap index files.
2. **Host CPU RAM OOMs**: Monotonic memory growth (reaching 2.2 TiB per host with aggressive worker configs) driven by asymmetric prefetch buffering across rare/frequent domains and glibc multi-thread heap fragmentation.
3. **Lustre MDS Deadlocks & Checkpoint Stalls**: Concurrent uncoordinated mmap file descriptor access across thousands of reader threads caused 5.6-minute Lustre Metadata Server (MDS) locks during Orbax checkpoint writes, breaching Megascale hang thresholds.
4. **Elastic Iterator Incompatibility**: `grain_use_elastic_iterator=True` was previously forbidden for dataset mixtures because `get_datasets()` returned an `IterDataset` rather than a `MapDataset`.

### Why This is a Good Solution
- **Consolidates Thread Pools**: Reduces internal reader thread pools from $D \times W$ down to $1 \times W$ (34 fewer thread pools per worker process, 272 fewer threads per host at $W=8$).
- **Stops Memory Growth**: Replaces 35 independent prefetch queues with a single on-demand stream, dropping the Host RSS memory growth slope by **>10x (91% reduction, from 0.130 MB/step down to 0.011 MB/step)**.
- **Improves Throughput**: Eliminates thread lock contention and reduces median step latency, increasing data throughput to **2.78M tokens/sec (+7.1% over baseline)**.
- **Unlocks Elastic Iterator for Mixtures (with Safety Validation)**: Because `get_datasets()` now returns a pure `MapDataset`, `grain_use_elastic_iterator=True` can now be used with multi-domain dataset mixtures when the mixture period is coprime to the shard count.
- **Compacts Checkpoint Payloads**: Checkpoint state metadata volume is reduced by **8.9x** (from 2,572 bytes down to 286 bytes) with deterministic 1:1 replay.

### Implementation Details
- In `src/maxtext/input_pipeline/grain_data_processing.py`:
  - Added shared helper `_mix_and_finalize()` used by both `mixture_config_path` and semicolon-delimited `grain_train_files`.
  - **Component-Wise Pre-Sharding**: Shards each constituent dataset *before* `grain.MapDataset.mix(dataset_list, weights)`. Because PyGrain's `MapDataset.mix` interleaves datasets with a deterministic periodic pattern (`P = sum(p_i) / gcd(p_i)`), sharding after mixing causes harmonic aliasing whenever `gcd(host_count, P) > 1` (which would starve hosts of domains). Pre-sharding ensures every host mixes all domains locally at the intended weights, while `SliceMapDataset`'s lazy index arithmetic introduces zero thread or memory overhead.
  - Converts to `to_iter_dataset()` **once** at the top level for the entire mixture (creating only 1 reader thread pool per worker), or returns the `MapDataset` directly if `elastic=True`.
  - Added `validate_mixture_elastic_compatibility()`: checks that `gcd(shard_count, P) == 1` when using `ElasticIterator`, raising a clear `ValueError` if an aliased configuration is requested.
- In `src/maxtext/configs/types.py`:
  - Removed the restriction in config validation forbidding `grain_use_elastic_iterator=True` when `grain_train_mixture_config_path` or semicolon-separated `grain_train_files` are set.
- In `tests/unit/grain_data_processing_test.py`:
  - Added `MixtureHostShardingTest` with 5 hermetic unit tests verifying:
    1. Every host sees all domains across aliasing-prone combinations (e.g., 2 domains on 2 hosts, 4 on 4, 8 on 8).
    2. Per-host domain proportions match configured weights within 2%.
    3. Hosts receive mutually disjoint data partitions.
    4. Elastic pipeline returns an unsharded `MapDataset`.
    5. `validate_mixture_elastic_compatibility` rejects aliased shard counts and accepts coprime ones.
  - Added unit test `GrainArrayRecordProcessingWithMixtureConfigAndElasticIteratorTest` to verify end-to-end mixture pipeline creation with `grain_use_elastic_iterator=True`.

### Shortcomings & Future Improvements
- Changing `grain_worker_count` dynamically on a restored checkpoint using standard `mp_prefetch` still encounters worker queue indexing constraints in PyGrain (`grain._src.python.dataset.transformations.interleave`). Full bidirectional worker elasticity ($W_1 \leftrightarrow W_2$) is achieved by enabling `grain_use_elastic_iterator=True`.

---

# Tests

Tested extensively on remote TPU v5p (`maxtext-single-host-3-v5p-8`) using a 35-domain ArrayRecord C4 mixture over 200 steps across worker counts $W \in \{2, 4, 8\}$:

| Metric | `IterDataset.mix` (Baseline) | `MapDataset.mix` (This PR) | Impact |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **OS Threads / Worker Process** | 166.0 | **132.0** | **34 fewer thread pools** per worker process |
| **Total OS Threads ($W=8$)** | 1,479 | **1,207** | **272 fewer threads** per host |
| **Memory Growth Rate ($W=8$)** | 0.1301 MB/step | **0.0116 MB/step** | **91.1% reduction** in memory growth rate |
| **Throughput ($W=8$)** | 2,532.7 samples/s | **2,713.0 samples/s** | **+7.1% throughput gain** (2.78M tokens/s) |
| **Checkpoint State Payload** | 2,572 bytes | **286 bytes** | **8.9x reduction** in metadata volume |
| **Deterministic Restore ($W=2 \to W=2$)** | Passed | **Passed** | Bitwise exact batch replay |

### Commands to Run Unit Tests
```bash
pytest tests/unit/grain_data_processing_test.py -k "Mixture"
```

title: Add free_kv_cache_during_weight_sync to the RL config and forward it to tunix
body:
## What

tunix frees the vLLM KV cache before every trainer->sampler weight sync and re-creates it afterwards. google/tunix#2231 made that optional (`RolloutConfig.rollout_vllm_free_kv_cache_during_weight_sync` -> `VllmConfig.free_kv_cache_during_weight_sync`): with it disabled the pool stays allocated and only its prefix-cache entries are reset.

MaxText cannot reach the option today: `MaxTextVllmRollout` builds its `VllmConfig` field by field and never passes it, and `RLConfig` rejects unknown keys.

This PR:
- adds the `RLConfig` field `free_kv_cache_during_weight_sync` (default `true` = tunix's default, so existing configs are unchanged) and declares it in `configs/post_train/rl.yml`;
- passes it into the tunix `RolloutConfig` through `_kwargs_supported_by`, so the currently pinned tunix (which predates the field) keeps working and the setting takes effect once the pin is bumped;
- forwards it from `MaxTextVllmRollout` into `VllmConfig` only when the rollout config carries the field **and** the installed `VllmConfig` accepts it, so a rollout config that has the attribute cannot break an older `VllmConfig`.

## Effect

Measured on a colocated Qwen3-0.6B GRPO run (64 tpu7x chips, `hbm_utilization_vllm=0.3`, two concurrent 20-step runs, TensorBoard `perf/train/global_step_time`, median of steps 3-20): 60.28 s with the default, 57.92 s with `free_kv_cache_during_weight_sync=false`. The run with the default logs `Deleting kv-cache` and `Reinitializing kv-cache` 21 times each; the run with `false` logs neither. HBM in use per chip goes 28.8 GiB -> 1.1 GiB -> 28.8 GiB around every sync with the default, and stays at 28.8 GiB with `false`.

The weight sync materializes a second copy of the sampler weights on HBM, so `false` is only safe when that copy fits next to the KV pool. The default `hbm_utilization_vllm` (0.72) leaves much less room than the 0.3 used above. Both config descriptions say so.

## Notes for the reviewer

- With the currently pinned tunix the option is a no-op: `_kwargs_supported_by` drops it and logs that the setting is ignored. It takes effect once the tunix pin includes google/tunix#2231.
- Both `update_params` overrides in `maxtext_vllm_rollout.py` delegate to tunix's `VllmSampler.update_params`, so all sync paths honor the option.
- `test_free_kv_cache_option_names_match_the_installed_tunix` is skipped in CI until the pin is bumped; I ran it locally against tunix main (61 passed).

## Tests

- `tests/post_training/unit/train_rl_test.py`
  - the field defaults to tunix's default and accepts an override;
  - `create_rl_components` (tunix pieces faked) passes `rollout_vllm_free_kv_cache_during_weight_sync` to `RolloutConfig` with the configured value when `RolloutConfig` declares it, and drops it cleanly for a `RolloutConfig` that predates it. This test fails if the `train_rl.py` forwarding is removed or the tunix field name is misspelt.
- `tests/post_training/unit/vllm_rollout_unroll_test.py`
  - `MaxTextVllmRollout` forwards both values into `VllmConfig`;
  - omits the kwarg when the rollout config lacks the field, and when `VllmConfig` is a strict class that does not accept it (fails with `TypeError` without the signature check);
  - pins the two tunix field names against the installed tunix (skipped while the pin predates them), since a misspelt name would be dropped without an error. The existing forwarding test now shares a construction helper with the new ones.
  - forwards the option when the `VllmConfig` signature cannot be inspected, matching what `_kwargs_supported_by` does.

Ran both files against the pinned-era tunix (60 passed, 1 skipped) and against tunix main (61 passed).

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/post_training/unit/vllm_rollout_unroll_test.py tests/post_training/unit/train_rl_test.py
```

title: Fixes three related correctness and stability defects in `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` (Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 hybrid GatedDeltaNet linear attention).
body:
Fixes three related correctness and stability defects in `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` (Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 hybrid GatedDeltaNet linear attention).

1. Left-padding corrupts the GDN recurrent state (`src/maxtext/models/qwen3.py`).
   `Qwen3NextGatedDeltaNet` applies a causal depthwise `conv1d` (kernel size K=4) to the concatenated `qkv` projection. Pad positions still carry non-zero `qkv` values, so on a left-padded sequence with P pad tokens the convolution window straddles the pad/real boundary and the first 3 real tokens receive a contribution from padding. `decoder_segment_ids` marks those tokens as valid, so nothing masks the contamination afterwards; it is written into the recurrent state S_t and carried forward across every GDN layer. The failure is quiet: no NaN, no shape error, finite loss. It only surfaces as the sampler and trainer disagreeing on the same tokens. Fix: zero pad positions before `conv1d`, after `conv1d`, on `query` in the existing Step C mask block (`key`/`value`/`g` were already masked), and after `out_proj`.

2. `l2norm` has a singular derivative at zero (`src/maxtext/layers/normalizations.py`).
   Masking pad rows to exactly 0.0 means `l2norm` is now legitimately evaluated at x = 0, where `rsqrt(0 + eps)` yields a Jacobian of 1/sqrt(eps) = 1000 for the default eps = 1e-6, and that gain compounds through the stacked GDN layers. Fix: the standard JAX double-`where` guard so zero-norm rows produce an exact 0.0 gradient.

3. Unsharded GDN forward pass crashes (pre-existing bug).
   `jax_chunk_gated_delta_rule` returns `None` for the final state when called without an `initial_state`. On the `self.mesh is None` path in train mode that `None` flows into `next_recurrent_state.astype(cfg.dtype)` and raises `AttributeError`. This reproduces on a clean upstream checkout, where it fails `test_gated_delta_net_structure` and `test_gated_delta_net_full`. Fix: only cast when a state was actually produced.

Adds `test_gated_delta_net_left_padding_invariance_and_gradients`, which feeds the layer a left-padded batch whose pad region is high-amplitude noise and asserts that pad positions come out exactly 0.0, that valid positions match an unpadded forward pass, and that input gradients are finite everywhere and exactly 0.0 on pad positions.

title: Restore checkpoint weights held outside the "params" collection
body:
# Description

Flax NNX derives variable collection names from the variable's class type via `variable_name_from_type`. Standard weights typed as `nnx.Param` reside in the `"params"` collection, while weights promoted to custom `nnx.Variable` subclasses—such as `MoEBiasVar` (`src/maxtext/layers/moe.py:364`), `Tid2EidVar` (`src/maxtext/layers/moe.py:360`), or `indexer_losses` (`src/maxtext/layers/attention_mla.py:80`)—reside in collections named after their class.

Previously, `load_params_from_path` silently failed to restore any weight residing in a non-`"params"` collection:

1. **Omission from request blueprint**: `_abstract_params` (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:387-399`) used an allowlist filtering strictly for `nnx.Param`, dropping custom variable subclasses entirely from the abstract params blueprint. Under `partial_load=True`, unrequested weights were never asked of Orbax, silently leaving them at unmaterialized initializers without raising an error.

2. **Dropping and tree-shifting in restore**: In `load_params_from_path` (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:855-888`), NNX restores requested only the `"params"` collection and unwrapped `restored_collection["params"]`. If a multi-collection checkpoint was loaded, non-`"params"` collections were dropped and the surviving tree shifted up one level, causing post-load mismatch validation to report the entire model as missing.

3. **MoE gate routing failure**: In `src/maxtext/layers/moe.py:443-448`, gate bias is initialized as `MoEBiasVar` for `deepseek3*`, `deepseek4*`, and `kimi-k2*`. Checkpoints written by the DeepSeek-V4 converter isolate this bias in a `MoEBiasVar` collection, while older checkpoints (e.g. DeepSeek-V3) store it flat under `"params"`. Consequently, neither layout restored properly into a model expecting `MoEBiasVar`, silently corrupting expert routing selection.

### Implementation

- **Denylist filtering in `_abstract_params`** (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:387-399`): Widens the filter from an `nnx.Param` allowlist to a denylist excluding only transient states (`nnx.RngState`, `nnx.Cache`, `nnx.Intermediate`, `nnx.BatchStat`), ensuring all persistent model variables are retained.

- **Collection-aware restore request** (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:855-888`): Groups abstract leaves by collection using `variable_name_from_type` and validates against checkpoint metadata. If metadata cannot be read, it is treated as `stored_collections = None` ("collections unknown") rather than defaulting to `"params"`, avoiding spurious drops on transient I/O failures.

- **Legacy collection aliasing** (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:123-190`, `src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:193-212`): `_alias_legacy_collections` checks whether a requested custom collection is missing on disk but exists within `params/params`. If found, it aliases those leaves into the `"params"` restore request so older checkpoints load into models with promoted variables. For Linen restores, `_unalias_legacy_collections` un-aliases leaves back into their respective collection mappings.

- **Multi-collection merging** (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:65-73`, `src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:948-957`): Merges restored collections recursively by path via `_deep_merge_dicts` so leaves across all collections populate `restored_weights`. Also updates `_linen_items_to_nnx` (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:317-323`) to merge custom collections into auxiliary state.

- **Validation & unconsumed audit** (`src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:215-239`, `src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:969-973`): Validates restored weights against the full model expectation (`want`) rather than post-filtered requests (preserving the LoRA/SFT exemption at `src/maxtext/common/checkpointing.py:94-96`). Introduces `_log_unconsumed_checkpoint_weights` using on-disk metadata (`audit_stored`) captured before request filtering, warning if checkpoint tensors were offered on disk but unconsumed.

### Checkpoint Layout Compatibility

| Layout | Structure | Status Before | Status After |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Flat** | `params/<weight>` | Raises mismatch | Raises mismatch (Pre-existing, out of scope) |
| **Legacy nested** | `params/params/...` | Worked | Works (Aliased onto `params` for models expecting custom collections) |
| **Split-by-collection** | `params/params/...` + `params/<Collection>/...` | Raised / Dropped | Works (Restores all collections and merges into model state) |

### Risk & Blast Radius

Low. Standard single-collection models (`nnx.Param` only) bypass aliasing entirely and follow the existing path. Models utilizing custom collections (`MoEBiasVar`, `Tid2EidVar`) are unblocked. Genuinely missing weights continue to raise `ValueError`, while unconsumed weights emit non-blocking warnings to avoid interrupting valid partial restores (e.g. LoRA or fine-tuning).

*Notice 1:* Once all tests pass, the "pull ready" label will automatically be assigned.
This label is used for administrative purposes. Please do not add it manually.

*Notice 2:* For external contributions, our settings currently require an approval from a MaxText maintainer to trigger CI tests.

# Tests

Added comprehensive CPU unit test suite in `tests/unit/checkpointing_collection_alias_test.py` (26 tests, 0 mocks on the save/load path) covering:

- **End-to-end save -> restore** (`TestRestoreAcrossCollections`, 8 tests): Verifies `save_params_to_path` -> `load_params_from_path` across flat, legacy nested, and split multi-collection checkpoint layouts, checking values and mismatch errors.
- **Collection aliasing & un-aliasing** (`TestAliasLegacyCollections`, 7 tests): Validates leaf movement into `params`, absent-weight preservation, skipping existing collections, partial-collection aliasing, unreadable metadata fallbacks, and Linen round-trip un-aliasing.
- **Dictionary utilities** (`TestDeepMergeDicts`, 4 tests; `TestLookupPath`, 3 tests): Tests recursive dictionary merging without mutation or sibling clobbering, and nested path lookup.
- **Abstract params filtering** (`TestAbstractParams`, 1 test): Verifies retention of custom variable classes and exclusion of transient states (`Cache`, `BatchStat`, `Intermediate`, `RngState`).
- **Unconsumed weight auditing** (`TestUnconsumedCheckpointWeights`, 3 tests): Validates warning generation for unrequested checkpoint tensors and silence when all weights are consumed.

### Reproduction Command

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/checkpointing_collection_alias_test.py -q
```
Result: `26 passed, 41 warnings in 13.53s`

   - Details the mathematical formulation of bi-level optimization (Inner local AdamW, pseudo-gradient computation, outer Nesterov momentum).
   - Derives operational Arithmetic Intensity ($AI = \frac{\text{FLOPs}}{\text{Bytes}}$) and physical network rooflines demonstrating how DiLoCo scales effective AI by a factor of $H$.
   - Formulates Streaming DiLoCo parameter fragmentation ($P$ fragments), staggered sync scheduling ($\Delta h = \lfloor H/P \rfloor$), asynchronous apply delay ($V$), and soft parameter blending ($\alpha$).
   - Explains the native JAX SPMD + NNX design (`DiLoCoTrainState`, `drjax.program` multi-placement, `FragmentedTreeManipulator`).
   - Clarifies the distinction between current SPMD algorithmic simulation and future MPMD multi-threading hardware overlap for $V$ and $\alpha$.
   - Integrated into `docs/reference/core_concepts.md`.

2. **DiLoCo Pre-training Tutorial ([`docs/tutorials/diloco_pretraining.md`](file:///usr/local/google/home/jzuo/maxtext/docs/tutorials/diloco_pretraining.md))**:

     - **Recipe 1**: Vanilla DiLoCo Multi-Slice Pre-training (Qwen3-8B on 2x `v5p-128`).
     - **Recipe 2**: Streaming DiLoCo Dense Pre-training (Qwen3-8B on 2x `v5p-128` with $H=37, P=37$).

   - Documents multi-replica Orbax checkpointing, automatic resumption, and single-slice parameter bootstrapping.

# Description

The weekly documentation link checker ([#5312](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/maxtext/issues/5312)) reported two findings. This PR addresses both.

**1. `docs/tutorials/posttraining/knowledge_distillation.md` — genuinely broken link (404)**

vLLM split their combined `recommended_models_features` page into two separate pages upstream, so the URL we link to no longer resolves:

| URL | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/tpu/en/latest/recommended_models_features` | 404 |
| `https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/tpu/en/latest/recommended_models/` | 200 |
| `https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/tpu/en/latest/features/` | 200 |

The surrounding sentence is about *which teacher models are supported on TPU vLLM*, so this points at `recommended_models/`.

**2. `docs/conf.py` — false positive**

The second finding was reported as `index.md:3444`, which is misleading: `docs/index.md` is only 51 lines. The link actually lives in `README.md`, whose `<!-- NEWS START -->` block is pulled into `docs/index.md` via an `{include}` directive, so the reported line number refers to the assembled document rather than a real source line.

The link itself is fine. GitHub returns a `302` to the login page for anonymous requests to `issues/new?template=...`, which is what the link checker sees. Rather than degrade a useful README link, this adds it to `linkcheck_ignore`, consistent with the existing entries for `pull/` and `blob/` URLs.

title: Derive fallback segment positions from an exclusive real-token count
body:
# Description

The `else` branch of `router_replay_gen_model_input_fn` numbers each packed segment from the running real-token count, sampled at that segment's first index. The sample is meant to be the segment's *pre-segment* total, but the count is inclusive of the index it is read at:

```python
-running = jnp.cumsum(token_mask != 0, axis=-1) - 1
+real = (token_mask != 0).astype(jnp.int32)
+preceding = jnp.cumsum(real, axis=-1) - real
```

An inclusive count equals the pre-segment total only when the segment's first slot holds a real token. When that slot is padding the count has not yet incremented, the subtraction comes out one short, and **every position in the segment is one too high**.

`token_mask = [0,1,1, 0,1,1]` with `segment_ids = [1,1,1, 2,2,2]`:

| | positions at the real tokens |
| --- | --- |
| before | `[1,2]` and `[1,2]` |
| after | `[0,1]` and `[0,1]` |

Counting real tokens *strictly before* each index makes the sample correct whether the first slot is real or padding. The difference is then non-negative by construction, so the `jnp.maximum(..., 0)` clamp is dead and is removed.

**Severity.** The error is a constant offset *within* a segment, not a scramble. RoPE attention scores depend on `pos_i - pos_j`, and cross-segment attention is masked, so the offset cancels and attention is unchanged. What it does change is each token's rotated hidden state, since RoPE rotates q/k by absolute position — and reproducing the rollout's hidden states is the purpose of router replay.

**Why the two fields are carried separately.** `segment_ids` and `segment_positions` drive independent mechanisms:

| field | model input | controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segment_ids` | `inputs_segmentation` | attention masking — which tokens may attend to which |
| `segment_positions` | `inputs_position` | RoPE — the absolute index each token is rotated by |

Neither is recoverable from the other in general. Padding is left at `0` in both, so a position alone cannot separate a padded slot from the first token of a segment; the ids are what distinguish the two. In the other direction, deriving positions from `segment_ids` requires assuming they are a dense `0..n-1` run over each segment's real tokens — which is precisely what this branch assumes. That assumption holds for `pack_bin` (`tunix/rl/packing.py:199-216`), which advances its cursor by exactly `prompt_len + completion_len` and writes `np.arange(n)`, but the payload contract does not require it: an internally padded segment breaks it, as does any rollout that numbered its tokens from a nonzero offset. The branch is a fallback for payloads that carry neither field, not a substitute for a producer that carries both.

**This is latent today, and that is worth stating plainly.** Reaching the branch requires `segment_positions` absent and `segment_ids` present. `pack_bin` is the only producer of packed `segment_positions` and always sets both; `tunix/rl/utils.py:494` and `tunix/experimental/orchestrator/batch_assembly.py:367` restack its rows rather than constructing positions themselves. Without `segment_ids` the function falls back to `segment_ids = token_mask`, under which every real-token segment starts on a real slot by construction. No current caller produces the triggering combination, so this prevents a future failure rather than repairing one that occurs today. Whether such a payload should instead be rejected outright rather than guessed at is a separate question this PR does not settle.

# Tests

`test_positions_restart_at_zero_when_a_segment_starts_padded` in `tests/post_training/unit/router_replay_engine_test.py`. It fails on the parent commit with `Lists differ: [1, 2] != [0, 1]` and passes here. It covers both one padded slot before a segment start and two, the latter being the case the one-short subtraction would leave at 1 rather than 0.

104 tests and 6 subtests pass on CPU in ~265 s:

```
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu python -m pytest \
  tests/post_training/unit/router_replay_engine_test.py \
  tests/post_training/unit/maxtext_engine_test.py \
  tests/post_training/unit/tunix_adapter_test.py \
  tests/post_training/unit/maxtext_engine_packing_test.py
```

No TPU run. This changes a position index on a branch no current caller reaches, not shapes or the composition of the packed step.

# Related

Same function as #5222, which fixes `targets_segmentation` on the line immediately below. The two were deliberately kept as separate PRs so each is reviewed on its own merits.

#5222 has since merged, and this branch is rebased onto it. It went as predicted: `maxtext_engine.py` auto-merged — the two changes are adjacent but independent — and the only conflict was in `router_replay_engine_test.py`, where both PRs add a test method at the same point. Resolved by keeping both, #5222's first. The `src/` diff above is now this change alone.

title: Fix: Numeric divergence between the mHC layer and its Pallas kernel
body:
Bug report: https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/maxtext/issues/5195

# Description

**Motivation:**
The reference path had its own `mapping` helper that cast `alpha_scale` and
`beta` down to `self.dtype` before computing `sigmoid(alpha_scale * h + beta)`,
while the Pallas path called `common.compute_sigmoid_gate`, which keeps the
scale and bias in float32. With `dtype: bfloat16` the two branches therefore
gated on different numbers, so toggling `use_mhc_pallas_kernel` changed the
layer's output beyond accumulation noise.

**Implementation:**
Drop `ManifoldConstrainedHyperConnections.mapping` and call the shared
`compute_sigmoid_gate` from both pre- and post-mapping, casting the float32
result back to `self.dtype` so the following GEMM is unchanged. Export the
helper from `maxtext.kernels.mhc` so the layer can reach it.

**Tests:**
- `test_pallas_kernel_matches_reference_path` runs the same weights through
  both branches and asserts they agree; the `_tpu` variant repeats it against
  the Mosaic-compiled kernel instead of interpret mode.
- `test_sigmoid_gate_computes_in_float32` pins the helper's precision directly,
  since the end-to-end comparison cannot resolve a bfloat16 regression there.
- Fold the four copies of the interpret-mode kernel patching into the
  `_interpreted_mhc_kernel` context manager, and the repeated module/MLP
  construction into `_build_mhc_and_mlp`.

# Tests

Unit tested on CPU and TPU v6e-1

title: Support quantized logits projection
body:
# Description

Under FP8 training (`quantization='fp8_full'`), the output vocabulary projection (`logits_dense`) previously remained in full precision (BF16).

This PR introduces `quantize_logits_proj=true` to quantize the logits projection via Qwix rule interception (`decoder/logits_dense.*`), with an optional `logits_proj_quant_calibration_method` override. For architectures with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) such as DeepSeek-V3, MTP modules reuse `decoder/logits_dense`, automatically extending FP8 quantization across all projection passes.

BUGS: b/559196820

## Changes
* **Config & Validation:** `src/maxtext/configs/base.yml`, `src/maxtext/configs/types.py`
  - Added `quantize_logits_proj` (default: `false`) and `logits_proj_quant_calibration_method` (default: `""`).
  - Added validations requiring `quantization='fp8_full'`, `logits_via_embedding=False` (untied embeddings), `num_vocab_tiling=1`, and `logits_dot_in_fp32=False`.
* **Qwix Interception:** `src/maxtext/layers/quantizations.py`
  - Prepended a dedicated `QtRule(module_path="decoder/logits_dense.*", ...)` targeting `dot_general` ahead of general layer rules.
  - Inherits the global calibration method by default or applies the specified override.
* **Documentation:** `docs/reference/core_concepts/quantization.md`
  - Documented flag behavior, calibration inheritance, architectural constraints, and MTP head reuse.
* **Testing:** `tests/unit/quantizations_test.py`
  - Added `LogitsProjQwixTest` verifying rule interception and calibration inheritance/override under CPU abstract evaluation.

## Details

1. **Theoretical Compute & Speedup:**
   - In large-vocabulary models like DeepSeek-V3 ($V = 129{,}280, d_{\text{model}} = 7{,}168$), the output head is a compute-heavy GEMM (~0.93B parameters, $2 \cdot d_{\text{model}} \cdot V$ FLOPs/token).
   - MTP reuses `decoder/logits_dense` via `apply_output_head`, accelerating both main and MTP projection passes ($(1 + M)$ invocations).
   - In DeepSeek-V3, the vocabulary projection accounts for ~2.5% of training FLOPs without MTP ($M=0$) and ~5.0% with MTP ($M=1$), yielding a theoretical roofline of ~1.2% to ~2.4% end-to-end speedup in FP8 (empirical gains are typically at most 1–2% due to unquantized softmax and communication overhead).


2. **Stability & Default Policy:**
   - The DeepSeek-V3 [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437) leaves the output head unquantized to safeguard cross-entropy convergence.
   - Other frameworks (such as [Megatron-LM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/40f68f976c525c1716bbb50879b63ad6c16b54c9/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py#L693-L696)) support quantizing the output projection (e.g., `fp8_output_proj` with block-scaled MXFP8 on GB300) when training stability permits.
   - `quantize_logits_proj` defaults to `false` to maintain baseline convergence by default while providing an opt-in knob for throughput optimization.


# Tests

### Unit Tests
Verified Qwix rule generation and interception under CPU abstract evaluation:
```bash
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu pytest tests/unit/quantizations_test.py -k "LogitsProjQwixTest"
```

### Rule Interception Tracing
Verified that Qwix intercepts `decoder/logits_dense` for both the main model (`dot_general0`) and MTP (`dot_general1`), [script](https://paste.googleplex.com/5583412799340544)
```
# quantize_logits_proj=true
[QWIX] module='decoder/logits_dense' op=dot_general0 rule=0
[QWIX] module='decoder/logits_dense' op=dot_general1 rule=0

# quantize_logits_proj=false
[QWIX] module='decoder/logits_dense' op=dot_general0 rule=None
[QWIX] module='decoder/logits_dense' op=dot_general1 rule=None
```

title: [training_engine] Honour ProfilerType.NONE in MicroStepProfiler
body:
MicroStepProfiler.__init__ decided whether to profile from profiler_steps alone. profiler_steps only sets the length of a profiling window and defaults to 5, so a run configured with profiler=ProfilerType.NONE still opened a trace at skip_first_n_steps_for_profiler.

Under Pathways that call goes through pathwaysutils' start_trace patch and raises "No profile started" from inside fwd_bwd, which takes down the trainer worker and then the orchestrator:

  micro_step_profiler.py:87 maybe_activate

profiler is the switch that enables profiling, so test it too.
