title: feat(ci): add e2e_test_scope input to TPU Docker images pipeline
body:
# Description

The TPU Docker Images Pipeline only had a boolean `run_e2e_tests` input, so a manual run for testing was all-or-nothing: it either ran both the pre-training and the post-training E2E suites, or neither. When you only touched one side, the other suite still consumed TPU capacity for hours.                                                                                
                                                                                                                                          
This replaces the boolean with an `e2e_test_scope` choice input and passes the selection down to the Airflow orchestrator DAG as `test_scope`:

| `e2e_test_scope` | Checkpoint Conversion | Pre-training | Post-training |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `none` (default) | ❌ *(job does not run)* | ❌ | ❌ |
| `all` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `pre-training` | ✅ | ✅ | ⏭️ *skipped* |
| `post-training` | ✅ | ⏭️ *skipped* | ✅ |


Notes on the implementation:

 - Scheduled runs hard-code `all` rather than relying on the input default, because the `inputs` context is empty for `schedule` events. Nightly behaviour is therefore unchanged.
 - `run_e2e_tests.yml` gains a `test_scope` input defaulting to `all`, so `release_pipeline.yml`, which does not pass it, keeps running the full suite.
- Checkpoint conversion always runs regardless of scope: both suites wait on its per-model task groups and share the converted checkpoints.
- The scope is also surfaced in the Airflow run note, so it is obvious from the DAG run list which suite a given run exercised.
  
Depends on ml-auto-solutions <https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/ml-auto-solutions/pull/1381>, which adds the `test_scope` param to `maxtext_e2e_tests`. That PR should be merged first; until it lands, the conf value is ignored and the DAG runs both suites as before, so merging in either order is safe.

# Tests

 Dispatched `TPU Docker Images Pipeline` from this branch and verified:
  
- `e2e_test_scope: none` -> the `run_e2e_tests` job is skipped.
- `e2e_test_scope: post-training` -> the job runs and the Airflow DAG run is created with `conf.test_scope = post-training`; in Airflow the pre-training trigger and its GitHub callback are `skipped` while checkpoint conversion and post-training run.

https://efdb2a1d6c2c435b8b7de77690c286a9-dot-us-central1.composer.googleusercontent.com/dags/maxtext_e2e_tests/grid?dag_run_id=auto_gha__35577762956__2026-09-21T08%3A31%3A18Z&task_id=trigger_tpu_pre_training&tab=logs

 DAG-side behaviour for each scope is covered in <https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/ml-auto-solutions/pull/1381>.

title: feat(kda): integrate KDA attention with tokamax backend and CP support
body:
# Description

This PR integrates **KDA (Kimi Delta Attention, a recurrent linear attention mechanism)** into MaxText end to end: the attention layer, the tokamax-backed Pallas TPU kernel, context parallelism (CP), and **decoder wiring via `attention_type='kda'`**. KDA updates its recurrent state with the Delta Rule:

```
S' = S * exp(g_t)
residual = v_t - k_t^T @ S'
S = S' + beta_t * k_t ⊗ residual
o_t = scale * q_t^T @ S
```

The layer follows the Megatron KDA reference and delegates kernel execution to tokamax's Pallas TPU implementation, keeping MaxText free of low-level kernel code.

## Key Changes

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `src/maxtext/layers/attention_kda.py` | New `KimiDeltaAttention` layer and `ShortConvolution`: QKV/beta/gate/output-gate projections, depthwise causal 1D convolution, SiLU activation, always-on QK L2 normalization, per-head RMSNorm + output gate, gate parameters `A_log` / `dt_bias` (matching the Megatron reference); also hosts `halo_exchange_for_conv` for CP |
| `src/maxtext/kernels/kda/` | New `chunk_kda` entry point + tokamax adapter: `[B,T,H,D]` ↔ `[H,B,T,D]` layout translation, lazy import of the KDA API, explicit `mosaic` implementation selection inside `shard_map` |
| `src/maxtext/common/common_types.py` | `AttentionType.KDA` |
| `src/maxtext/configs/types.py` | New `KdaAttention` config (`linear_conv_kernel_dim`, `use_kda_safe_gate`, `kda_lower_bound`, reserved `use_kda_lora`) + validators; `attention_type` Literal gains `"kda"`; `attention_type='kda'` with `scan_layers=true` is rejected at config time |
| `src/maxtext/configs/base.yml` | KDA flags registered; `attention_type` supported list |
| `src/maxtext/layers/nnx_decoders.py` | `NNXDecoderLayer` gains a per-layer `attention_type` override and a KDA branch: builds `KimiDeltaAttention` (no KV cache — recurrent state is carried by the kernel); non-KDA types are untouched |
| `tests/unit/kda_attention_test.py` | Layer/kernel/CP suite (see below) |
| `tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py` | Decoder-integration suite: config guards + a real-decoder training run |
| `docs/reference/kda_cp_support.md` | Design doc, linked into the Reference toctree |

## Using KDA

Select it like any other attention variant — this mirrors how `attention_type='mla'` is consumed:

```yaml
attention_type: kda
scan_layers: false        # required (KDA layers are not validated in scanned stacks yet)
use_kda_safe_gate: true   # recommended: bounded-decay gate, keeps the recurrence stable
kda_lower_bound: -5.0     # common choice, required in [-5, 0) when the safe gate is on
```

Notes:
- KDA always L2-normalizes Q/K — this is part of the KDA architecture (the Delta-Rule recurrence diverges with unbounded q/k), independent of the shared `use_qk_norm` flag which belongs to dot-product attention.
- `context_parallel_load_balance` is rejected with KDA+CP (token order is load-bearing for the recurrent state).
- KDA has no KV cache; autoregressive decoding is not implemented yet (raises a clear `NotImplementedError`). Train/prefill paths are supported.

## Context Parallelism Support

- The CP mesh axis is taken from `cfg.context_sharding` (default `"context"`; `"expert"` works for expert-as-context) and is threaded consistently through the conv halo exchange, the T-axis partition-spec injection, and `ContextParallelMetadata`
- Under CP without user segments, an all-ones segment tensor is synthesized outside `shard_map` so the kernel can always derive per-rank `cu_seqlens` / chain fields
- `ShortConvolution` pulls `kernel_size-1` left-context tokens from the previous CP rank via `ppermute` inside a dedicated `shard_map`; a clear `ValueError` guards the `kernel_size-1 > T_local` case (multi-rank receptive fields are not implemented)

## Tests and Validation

**Unit tests — 35 TPU tests + 23 CPU tests, all passing** (4×TPU v6e, 2026-09-04):

- Layer/kernel: forward/backward (activations + weights), determinism, padding, packed-segment isolation (cross-row and within-row), precision vs a pure-XLA recurrent reference (FP32/BF16, ULP-based fallback)
- CP: kernel-level equivalence parametrized CP=2/CP=4, CP backward, full-layer CP without segments (dummy synthesis path), **full-layer CP with real packed segments** (segment spanning the rank boundary + boundary exactly at the split; fwd + input/weight grads vs non-CP), oversized-halo rejection, load-balance rejection, CP metadata-missing refusal
- Composition: full-layer **Mosaic vs tokamax XLA reference parity** (same weights, fwd + grads)
- Kernel guards: `initial_state` / `output_final_state` rejected with clear errors
- Markers: `tpu_only` is applied per-test, so the pure config/pure-op tests also run in regular CPU CI

**Decoder integration** (`tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py`):

- CPU-runnable: config acceptance, `scan_layers` guard, dispatch of `NNXDecoderLayer` to `KimiDeltaAttention` (and unchanged default for other types)
- TPU: a real-decoder training run (`decoder_block=default`, 2 layers, delayed-copy task — i.i.d. tokens with `t[i] = t[i-delay]`, `delay=5` beyond the conv receptive field, so only the recurrent state can solve it; masked loss): **loss collapses from 5.28 to < 1.0 in 400 steps** through the actual decoder

### Reproducing

On a TPU host (Python ≥ 3.12; verified on 4×TPU v6e):

```bash
# 1. TPU-capable JAX (validation used JAX 0.11.0 + libtpu 0.0.44.1)
pip install "jax[tpu]" -f https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/libtpu_releases.html

# 2. MaxText with TPU dependencies
pip install -e <maxtext checkout>
pip install -r <maxtext checkout>/src/dependencies/requirements/generated_requirements/tpu-requirements.txt

# 3. tokamax with the KDA kernels — the KDA API has landed on openxla/tokamax
#    main but no release contains it yet; install from source:
git clone https://github.com/openxla/tokamax.git && pip install -e tokamax
#    (or the equivalent branch validated here: -b antgroup/kda-pallas-kernel, tip 939da5c)

# 4. Tests (kernel/CP tests are tpu_only and skip cleanly elsewhere)
pytest tests/unit/kda_attention_test.py tests/unit/kda_decoder_integration_test.py -v
```

## Dependencies

- The KDA kernels come from [openxla/tokamax#1103](https://github.com/openxla/tokamax/pull/1103) (Kimi Delta Attention Pallas kernels, by @Fred33146). **Status**: the code has landed on openxla/tokamax `main` (signature-compatible with this PR's adapter, verified), but **no public tokamax release contains it yet**. MaxText's pin therefore cannot express the dependency; the adapter imports the KDA API lazily, so installs without it are unaffected until KDA is actually used (clear `ImportError` with instructions at that point). Once the first release ships, the `tokamax>=` pin and derived requirement files will be bumped.
- Validated with JAX 0.11.0 + libtpu 0.0.44.1

## Hardware / Shape Constraints (mosaic kernel)

The adapter selects the `"mosaic"` Pallas implementation explicitly (no silent fallback). Constraints — surfaced as clear `NotImplementedError`s from tokamax at bind time:

- TPU generation ≥ 6 (validated on v6e)
- Key dimension ≤ 256
- Under CP: key and value head dims must be multiples of 128
- Sequence length padded internally to a multiple of chunk size 64

## Known Limitations / Follow-ups

- Autoregressive/inference path not implemented (train/prefill only; AR raises a clear error)
- `initial_state` / `output_final_state` not yet supported (explicit `NotImplementedError`)
- `scan_layers` must be `false` with `attention_type='kda'` (scanned KDA stacks not validated yet)
- bf16 training-recipe tuning for KDA models (the integration test validates in fp32 with the safe gate)
- Hybrid per-layer KDA + softmax models (e.g. Ling-style interleaving) and a production KDA model config
- tokamax version pin bump once the first public release with the KDA API ships

Flash attention: replicate the kv head axis for MQA
body:
# Description

Changes flash attention to replicate the K/V head axis for MQA when the mesh shards that axis. This prevents a trace failure from applying query-head sharding to K/V.

The fix applies only to MQA, where `num_kv_heads=1`. It does not replicate the K/V head axis for GQA, because each shard would pair its local query heads with the wrong K/V heads and silently compute incorrect attention. Replicating 2 K/V heads across 4 head shards produced output differing from the dense reference by up to 5.9 on an 8-device CPU mesh.

title: fix(elastic): Recover from the latest complete checkpoint, and actually restore it
body:
# Description

A slice went down while step 1820 was being written, and `pw-snp-2x64-0827-7` then tried to restore that unfinished checkpoint and died with `ValueError: Found incomplete checkpoint at .../checkpoints/1820`. The JobSet restarted, a fresh `CheckpointManager` listed the finalized steps and resumed from 1800, so the run finished on its own — but 16 minutes passed between checkpoints 1800 and 1820, where 20 steps normally take ~28 s.

Four problems in the elastic snapshot recovery path, in the order they bite:

- **The step cache keeps a save that failed.** Orbax's `CheckpointManager` records a step as soon as the blocking half of `save()` returns, and only `wait_until_finished()` evicts it when the background commit fails. `cancel_checkpoint_manager()` detaches the finalize thread, so nothing evicts the step when the commit fails a few seconds later — which is exactly what happens when the slice that was writing it goes away. `latest_step()` then hands back a step whose directory has no `commit_success.txt`, and the persistent-checkpoint fallback in `recover()` restores it. The same stale entry makes `should_save()` refuse every step at or below it: after this run rolled back to 1615, the saves at 1620, 1640 and 1660 were skipped without a word. `cancel_checkpoint_manager()` now reloads the finalized steps from storage, which is what a fresh manager does anyway — the restarted head in this incident listed 91 steps and picked 1800.
- **The NNX restore was a no-op.** `recover()` handed the `TrainStateNNX` module to `load_state_if_possible()`, which maps an NNX state out of the Linen on-disk layout only when it is given an `nnx.State`. With the module, the partial restore matched no checkpoint keys and returned the freshly initialized state unchanged. The incident log shows it at 08:50: `restoring from this run's directory step 1600`, then `Resuming safely at step 0`. A tpu7x run reproduced it, and it means a "successful" fallback silently threw away every step of training. Pass `nnx.state(state)`.
- **An old snapshot won against a newer checkpoint.** In-memory snapshots are skipped while a persistent save is in flight (29ef09892). With `checkpoint_period=20` a save takes ~25 s and 20 steps take ~24 s, so a save is nearly always in flight and the only snapshot left is the one taken at startup: all 41 snapshot attempts between steps 1620 and 1820 were skipped. `recover()` preferred it anyway, rolling the run back from step 240 to 0, and later from 1824 to 1615, while checkpoints 220 and 1800 sat finished on GCS. It now restores the latest finalized checkpoint when that is newer than the snapshot, and falls back to the snapshot if the restore fails; a slice failure during the restore still restarts the recovery.
- **The snapshot resume step was off by one.** Snapshots taken in the train loop hold the state after their step's update, but `recover()` resumed at the snapshot's own step, so that step ran a second time and the loop counter stayed one behind the optimizer step. After restoring the snapshot taken at 1615 the job ran 1615 again, and the next scale-up resumed at optimizer step 1666 with the loop about to run 1665. Resume from the restored step counter, as the checkpoint and resharding paths already do.

FIXES: b/553535006

# Tests

**Unit.** New `tests/unit/elastic_recover_test.py`: six cases over a tiny NNX `TrainStateNNX`, with Pathways, mesh setup and compilation mocked but checkpoints saved and restored for real, covering snapshot-newer, checkpoint-newer, either one failing, and a slice failure during the restore. New case in `tests/unit/checkpointing_test.py` drives a real async save whose commit fails after `cancel_checkpoint_manager()` and asserts the failed step is gone from the cache and `should_save()` is free again. Every new assertion fails with its own fix reverted. 86 tests pass across `tests/unit/{checkpointing,elastic_recover,elastic_utils,train_nnx}_test.py` on orbax-checkpoint 0.12.1 (the version in the incident image) and 0.12.4.

**Hardware.** 2 × tpu7x `2x2x1` on `bodaborg-tpu7x-spot-sps`, llama3.1-8b, `checkpoint_period=20`, the same `20260826_3ae3` images with these four files mounted over them. `cloud_pathways_server` on one worker was killed while a checkpoint save was in flight, the way the team simulates a slice loss.

| | incident, no fixes | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `latest_step()` after the cancel | 1820, the save that had failed | 20, the last finalized step |
| restore source | snapshot at 1615, then `ValueError` on 1820 | checkpoint 20 |
| resume step | 0, freshly initialized weights (08:50) | 21, loss 9.26 → 8.79 against 9.10 → 9.01 before the failure |
| saves while degraded | 1620, 1640, 1660 skipped | checkpoint 40 written on the surviving slice |

Initial loss is 12.2 for reference, so the restored weights are the checkpoint's, not an init. The first hardware run carried only three of these four commits and resumed at step 0 with init weights; that is how the no-op restore was found.

**Seen while testing, not addressed here (Pathways side).** The first step after a recovery never finished when the killed slice rejoined while that step was still compiling, and Pathways logged it moving `jit_train_step` onto the returning slice; the incident shows the same shape of hang after its scale-up. Separately, a save on the degraded mesh hung while the peer's server sat stopped rather than crashed, which a real crash may not reproduce.

title: fix(optimizer): guard against NaN/Inf gradients and norm spikes
body:
### Summary
This PR adds guards against non-finite gradients (`NaN`/`Inf`) and severe gradient norm spikes in both the `MaxTextTrainingEngine` and `skip_step_on_spikes` optimizer wrapper:

1. **`MaxTextTrainingEngine` (`maxtext_engine.py`)**:
   - Computes `is_finite = jnp.isfinite(grad_norm)` and optionally enforces `grad_norm <= max_grad_norm_spike`.
   - When non-finite or spiked (`skip_step_on_nan` default: `True`), zeroes out gradients passed to clipping and optimizer to prevent NaN division/propagation.
   - Restores the original un-updated parameters and optimizer state (`new_state_pure = jnp.where(should_skip, state_pure, new_state_pure)`), ensuring neither model weights nor optimizer moments are corrupted.
   - Emits `step_skipped = 1.0` in step metrics.

2. **`skip_step_on_spikes` (`optimizers.py`)**:
   - Enforces `is_finite` check on both `loss` and `grad_norm`.
   - Ensures warmup (`is_warmup`) never bypasses `is_finite`, preventing early NaNs from advancing weights.
   - Prevents non-finite values from poisoning the rolling statistics buffer (`losses` and `grad_norms`), preserving subsequent training stability.

3. **Config & Types (`base.yml`, `types.py`)**:
   - Added `skip_step_on_nan: bool = True` and `max_grad_norm_spike: NonNegativeFloat = 0.0`.

4. **Unit Tests (`optimizers_test.py`, `train_nnx_test.py`)**:
   - Added tests covering NaN loss/grad_norm during warmup, NaN buffer isolation, and parameter preservation.

title: fix(dependencies): fix vulnerabilities for pre-training and post-training Docker images
body:
# Description


Fix container security vulnerabilities (Critical, High, Medium, and Low OS CVEs) for both TPU pre-training and post-training Docker images:

https://pantheon.corp.google.com/artifacts/docker/tpu-prod-env-multipod/us/maxtext-images/maxtext_jax_stable/sha256:9119db5ea26713230673045e7dcf19750b95d5003a9d35be417d0e798e7abda7;tab=vulnerabilities

- **Upgrade Base Image to Debian 13 (`python:3.12-slim-trixie`)**: Upgrades the base image in `maxtext_tpu_dependencies.Dockerfile` and `clean_py_env.Dockerfile` from `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` to `python:3.12-slim-trixie`, resolving all 7 Critical OS CVEs (in `perl`, `openssl`, and `zlib`) as well as High/Medium/Low CVEs in `openssl`, `perl`, `expat`, `util-linux`, `pam`, and `curl`.

- **Preserve GCC 12 Compiler Compatibility**: Pins `/usr/bin/gcc` and `/usr/bin/g++` to `gcc-12` and `g++-12` via `update-alternatives` so C/C++ extensions (such as vLLM in post-training) continue to build with the exact same compiler version as on `bookworm`.

- **Replace Deprecated `apt-key` with `gpg --dearmor`**: Replaces `apt-key` (removed in Debian Trixie) with `gpg --dearmor` into `/usr/share/keyrings/cloud.google.gpg` across `maxtext_tpu_dependencies.Dockerfile`, `clean_py_env.Dockerfile`, and `setup.sh`.

- **Avoid Unnecessary Recommended Packages in `setup.sh`**: Adds `--no-install-recommends` to `apt-get install` in `setup.sh` to prevent pulling unnecessary packages (`openssh-client`, `xauth`, `libx11`) and their associated CVEs.

# Tests

- Built both `WORKFLOW=pre-training` and `WORKFLOW=post-training` TPU Docker images locally via `bash src/dependencies/scripts/docker_build_dependency_image.sh`.  

- Verified package resolution and imports (`import jax, flax, maxtext, vllm, tunix, qwix`) inside the built containers.

- Executed unit tests inside the built containers (`pytest tests/unit/pyconfig_test.py` and `pytest tests/post_training/unit/train_rl_test.py`).
